title: Context-aware probe sampler for tracing hotpaths and perf regression detection
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Tracing on high‑QPS inference hotpaths is still a source of measurable CPU and allocation overhead. Existing sampling is effective at reducing volume but lacks context-awareness (e.g., temporally clustered latency spikes, request type, and tenant-specific noise). We need a lightweight mechanism that injects conditional probes (very small, low-allocation spans and metadata) to catch long-tail regressions and provide high‑signal samples for post‑hoc debug while keeping hotpath overhead negligible.

Proposal: Implement a context-aware probe sampler that runs a tiny conditional decision in the tracing hotpath to occasionally record a minimal 'probe span' (no heavy attribute encoding, no stack capture). Probe decisions combine three inexpensive signals: local latency percentile (moving window), request route classifier (hot vs background), and recent error-rate delta. The sampler should adapt weights over time (more probes when moving percentiles rise or errors increase) and support shadow injection to capture full spans asynchronously for a small subset of probes. This hybrid approach reduces baseline tracing overhead while retaining high-fidelity samples when the system shows anomalous behavior.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end implementation behind feature flag 'probe-sampler' that can be toggled per-service and per-region.
Probe spans < 120 bytes on average (no large attribute blobs) and add <1% CPU overhead at 95th percentile on a 100k QPS benchmark compared to tracing-off baseline.
Adaptive sampling reacts within 60s to a moving‑percentile shift > 10% and increases probe rate to capture additional samples.
Shadow/full-span capture for probes limited to 0.1% of requests under normal conditions, configurable per-service.
New dashboards and alerts showing probe-rate, probe-latency-percentiles, probe-to-full-span ratio, and detection events for perf regressions.
Canary rollout to 10% traffic in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 with monitored gate metrics before wider ramp.
Automated CI tests that assert probe sampling logic and that enabling/disabling the flag does not change primary request latency beyond noise.
implementation_notes: Hotpath decision must be allocation-free: use bitfield counters and atomic increments; avoid string allocations and map lookups.
Probe span is a lightweight marker span with a single enum attribute describing probe type (latency-alert | error-signal | periodic), timestamp, and compressed route id (uint32).

Shadow capture pipeline implemented as asynchronous worker: on probe decision, enqueue a reference to request context (opaque id) to a bounded ring buffer; worker resolves and records full span from sidecar or agent process to avoid hotpath work.
Adaptive controller runs off‑hotpath (background goroutine) and updates three weights: latency_weight, error_weight, route_weight; controller exposes an atomic u32 for hotpath to read thresholds.
Fallback: if probe pipeline is overloaded, degrade to pure lightweight probes (no shadow capture) and emit a 'probe_dropped' metric.
Config surface: per-service sample_rate_min, sample_rate_max, shadow_fraction, moving_window_seconds (default 60s), percentile_threshold (default 95th).
Cross-team touchpoints: SRE (Marco Chen) for rollout and alerts; Observability PM (Priya Singh) for dashboard acceptance; SDK owners for span format changes.
testing_plan: Unit tests for decision logic under synthetic moving percentile inputs (edge cases: jittery latency, burst errors).
Microbenchmarks: measure allocations and CPU per-request with and without probes at low/medium/high QPS profiles.
Integration test that validates shadow capture enqueues and worker drains within configured SLO under synthetic load.
Chaos test: simulate probe worker outage and assert system falls back gracefully and emits 'probe_dropped' metric.
End-to-end perf test: 100k QPS loadtest comparing default sampling -> probe-sampler enabled -> probe+shadow enabled.
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated rollout. Step 1: Enable flag for internal staging services; monitor for 72 hours.
Step 2: Canary to 10% traffic in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for 48 hours; check gate metrics (CPU overhead <2%, probe_dropped <0.5%).
Step 3: Gradual increase to 50% regionally with automated ramp if gate metrics hold, otherwise revert to last good state.
Step 4: Global enable for non-critical tenants, staggered by SLA tier. Critical tenants opt-in via dedicated config.
rollback_plan: Flip feature flag off globally (fast path).
If flag cannot be toggled quickly due to config propagation, temporarily increase sample_rate_min to zero and shadow_fraction to 0 to stop extra work.
If rollback due to dataplane errors, coordinate with infra to scale down workers or isolate the worker queue.
related_artifacts: GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5021 (hotpath guards and atomic counters)
comments: 2025-02-18 Ava Martinez: Created ticket after postmortem review identified gap in high-signal trace capture during short-lived latency spikes.

2025-02-21 Rohan Patel: Spike complete — implemented prototype of atomic decision bit and tiny probe span. Microbenchmarks show ~0.6% CPU overhead at 50k QPS. Pushed branch for initial review (see PR #1482).
2025-02-25 Priya Singh (PM): Reviewed prototype; requested configurable shadow_fraction and clearer dashboard readouts for probe vs full spans.
2025-02-28 Marco Chen (SRE): Noted that worker ring buffer needs explicit backpressure metric and a bounded retry policy. Asked to add 'probe_dropped' metric.

2025-03-03 QA: Ran integration with shadow worker; observed shadow enqueue latency spike under bursty traffic — increasing worker pool reduced latency but increased memory. Decided to keep default shadow_fraction at 0.1% and add adaptive backoff to the worker.
2025-03-04 Rohan Patel: Addressed feedback, added probe_dropped metric, implemented adaptive controller tuning endpoint, and updated design docs. Ready for canary once runtime-1.20 branch is cut.
